comments.note: The matchRoute() function uses a documented segment-count ordering comment block (lines ~190-200) to warn future maintainers about shadowing risk. The new GET /api/orchestrator/queue route (rest.length === 2, rest[0] === 'orchestrator') has no current sibling routes at that segment count, so there is no ordering concern. The comment block is already a useful convention — no change needed.

POST /api/orchestrator/start uses the module-level WORKSPACE_ROOT constant imported at the top of server.ts, consistent with how ORCHESTRATOR_LOGS_DIR is used. This keeps workspaceRoot out of the matchRoute() signature while remaining testable at the api.ts handler level. Clean pattern.

summary: All four orchestrator routes verified in server.ts: GET /api/orchestrator/queue (matchRoute), POST /api/orchestrator/start (special-case with body parsing), POST /api/orchestrator/kill/:id and POST /api/orchestrator/dismiss/:id (special-case blocks with decodeURIComponent).
TypeScript compiles cleanly (tsc --noEmit produces no output).
All 2096 tests pass across 66 test files including 23 tests in api-orchestrator.test.ts (handler-level AC) and 642 tests across the entire GUI suite — no regressions.

AC verification: (1) All four routes dispatch to correct handlers ✓; (2) POST start body parsed with readBody + JSON.parse, VALIDATION_ERROR on invalid JSON ✓; (3) :id extracted via path.slice + decodeURIComponent ✓; (4) WORKSPACE_ROOT imported at module level, always available ✓; (5) No regressions ✓.

Edge-case analysis: empty/traversal IDs (handled by handler's NOT_FOUND guard), missing trailing slash on kill/dismiss paths (falls through to matchRoute → 404), invalid JSON body on start (400 VALIDATION_ERROR), double-encoded path traversal (decodes to / which handler rejects). All paths safe.

comments.note: POST /api/orchestrator/kill and /dismiss without a trailing slash (e.g. /api/orchestrator/kill without /:id) fall through to matchRoute() which returns null → 404. This is correct behaviour, but worth noting for documentation consistency.

No server-level integration test for the orchestrator routes in server.ts (handleRequest). The handler-level tests in api-orchestrator.test.ts provide strong coverage. Adding one integration test exercising handleRequest directly (as done in api.test.ts) would give defence-in-depth but is not a hard blocker.

summary: Reviewed mcp-server/gui/server.ts (sole modified file). 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (pre-existing readBody size-cap gap, noted). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Info — A01 (Broken Access Control): Static file serving uses resolve(filePath) + startsWith(PUBLIC_DIR) containment guard (server.ts ~line 478). Path traversal outside PUBLIC_DIR is correctly rejected with 404. PASS.

Info — A01 (Broken Access Control): POST /api/orchestrator/start planPath traversal: user-supplied planPath is passed through resolve() then checkPathPrefix() in orchestrator-manager.ts (~line 556). The root path is normalised to always end with '/' before the startsWith check, preventing false matches against sibling directories (e.g. /workspace-evil). Orchestrator is not spawned if check fails. PASS.

Info — A01 (Broken Access Control): Queue entry IDs for kill/dismiss: assertSafeQueueId (api.ts line 127) rejects empty, '/', or '..' values. The ID is used only for string equality lookup in the in-memory queue array — it is never concatenated into a file path. The per-plan lock file removal uses entry.planPath from the trusted queue file, not the user-supplied ID. PASS.
Info — A03 (Injection): POST /api/orchestrator/start spawns via spawn(bin, [resolvedPlan], ...) with arguments passed as an array, bypassing the shell entirely. No shell injection vector. PASS.

Medium — A04 (Insecure Design): readBody() (server.ts ~line 168) buffers the full request body in memory with no size limit. The new POST /api/orchestrator/start route adds one more call site to this pre-existing pattern (also used by PUT /api/config, PATCH /api/projects/:slug, POST /api/projects/:slug/reset). A local network client or a bug in the front-end could send an arbitrarily large body, causing unbounded memory growth. For a localhost-only dev tool the exploitability is low, but a Content-Length or cumulative byte cap (e.g. 1 MB) would eliminate the risk entirely. Recommendation: add a maxBytes guard inside readBody(). Does not block approval for this WP.

Info — A05 (Security Misconfiguration): CORS origin is locked to http://localhost:${port} (not a wildcard). Security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, CSP) are applied to all response paths including the new 204 dismiss response and OPTIONS preflight. Internal errors log to stderr only — no stack traces are returned to the client. PASS.
Info — A06 (Vulnerable & Outdated Components): WP-009 introduced no new npm dependencies. Only server.ts routing was modified. PASS.

summary: WP-009 code review: PASS with one Fix-Forward applied. Reviewed mcp-server/gui/server.ts — all four orchestrator route additions (GET /api/orchestrator/queue in matchRoute(), POST /api/orchestrator/start, POST /api/orchestrator/kill/:id, POST /api/orchestrator/dismiss/:id as special-case blocks in handleRequest()) are correctly implemented. Implementation is consistent with established server patterns: body-parsing routes go to special-case blocks, parameter-free routes go to matchRoute(). Error handling, CORS/security headers (including on the 204 dismiss response), and WORKSPACE_ROOT usage all follow existing conventions. Fix-Forward applied: extended the route-map comment block in matchRoute() to enumerate the three new orchestrator POST routes handled outside it, maintaining the existing maintainability convention. TypeScript compiles cleanly after the edit. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: Extended the route-map comment block at the bottom of matchRoute() (lines ~460-475) to enumerate the three new orchestrator POST routes (start, kill/:id, dismiss/:id) that are handled in handleRequest() rather than matchRoute(). The existing block only mentioned /api/config and /api/projects/:slug/reset; the new routes follow the same pattern but were not listed. Change is comment-only — no behavioural effect. TypeScript still compiles cleanly.

kill/:id and dismiss/:id are POST routes that don't require body parsing, yet they are wired as special-case blocks in handleRequest() rather than in matchRoute(). Functionally equivalent and consistent with path.slice() extraction used for PATCH /api/projects/:slug, but segment-based matching in matchRoute() would be marginally more precise (rejects extra path segments via rest.length check). Not a blocking concern for a localhost-only dev tool.

The handleRequest() special-case section now has 9 early-return blocks before the matchRoute() fallback. If more orchestrator routes are added (e.g. a GET /api/orchestrator/status/:id that needs no body but is kept alongside its siblings), a sub-router for /api/orchestrator/* could improve organisation. Not an issue at current scale.
